title: Vasa (ship)

paragraphs: Vasa was a Swedish warship built between 1626 and 1628 on the orders of King Gustavus Adolphus, who demanded heavier firepower partway through construction.
Shipwrights fitted 64 bronze cannons across 2 enclosed gun decks, leaving the tall hull dangerously top-heavy with insufficient stone ballast below the waterline.
On 10 August 1628, Vasa departed Stockholm harbor on her maiden voyage with lower gunports propped open to fire a ceremonial salute.
After sailing roughly 1,300 meters, a light gust heeled the ship to port, seawater flooded the open lower gunports, and Vasa sank in 32 meters of water with 30 lives lost.
Protected from shipworms by the cold brackish Baltic Sea, Vasa was raised largely intact in 1961 after 333 years on the seabed.
